Collect Pool Results as Promises

Source: R/promise.R
mizu_collect_all_async.Rd

mizu_collect_all_async() and mizu_collect_any_async() are the async counterparts of mizu_collect_all() and mizu_collect_any(): each returns immediately with exactly one promises::promise() per collection — no per-task promise is ever allocated. On each wake the pool checks for newly finished tasks, and when the collection completes the sync version's result assembly runs once and resolves the promise.

Usage

mizu_collect_all_async(tasks, timeout = Inf)

mizu_collect_any_async(tasks, timeout = Inf)

# S3 method for class 'mizu_task'
as.promise(x)

# S3 method for class 'mizu_task'
is.promising(x)

# S3 method for class 'mizu_map'
as.promise(x)

# S3 method for class 'mizu_map'
is.promising(x)

Arguments

tasks

a non-empty list of task handles from mizu_submit() on the same pool handle.

timeout

seconds after which the promise rejects with the mizu_timeout classed error; nothing is consumed. Inf (the default) waits indefinitely.

x

for the as.promise methods: a task handle, or a map handle from mizu_map() / mizu_map_run().

Value

A promises::promise(): collect-all resolves a plain list of the task values in the order of tasks (names carried); collect-any resolves list(index, value).

Details

The behavior mirrors the sync functions. Collect-all resolves in input order with names carried; the first erroring handle by position rejects with index (only that handle consumed, the rest collectible). Collect-any resolves list(index, value) for the first terminal task, a raised outcome rejecting with the index field. A timeout rejects with the mizu_timeout classed error and consumes nothing. When a collection finishes — resolved, rejected, or timed out — every handle in it is released: handles whose results were not consumed become blocking-collectible again.

A task with a promise attached — or part of a pending collection — refuses mizu_collect(), mizu_collect_any(), mizu_collect_all(), and a second promise, with an error naming the pending consumer. mizu_cancel() stays allowed: the cancel publishes, and the pending promise rejects with mizu_error_cancelled.

Requires the later and promises packages.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive() && requireNamespace("promises", quietly = TRUE)
library(promises)
p <- mizu_pool(2L)
ts <- list(
  total = mizu_submit(p, sum(x), x = runif(10)),
  label = mizu_submit(p, "done")
)
mizu_collect_all_async(ts) %...>% print()
later::run_now()
mizu_pool_stop(p)
}
